title: Bay of Pigs invasion
summary: On 17 April 1961 Brigade 2506, about 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles launched from Guatemala, landed at the Bay of Pigs on Cuba's southern coast. Cuban forces under Fidel Castro defeated them within two days; most were imprisoned. The failure strengthened Castro, who moved toward socialism and closer ties with the Soviet Union.

uncertainty.note: The Office of the Historian gives the landing as 17 April 1961 and the defeat within two days; the CIA page gives 17 April as D-Day. The end date 19 April is the span of "within two days" and is not itself stated on the page.

as_recorded.value: landed at the Bay of Pigs on April 17, 1961 ... defeated within 2 days

where.modern_name: Bay of Pigs (Bahía de Cochinos), Matanzas Province, Cuba
where.historical_name: Bay of Pigs, southern coast of the Republic of Cuba

importance.justification: A failed US-backed invasion that deepened the US-Cuba break and fed into Operation Mongoose and the 1962 missile crisis.

audience_note: Armed invasion with deaths and mass imprisonment; the numbers of killed and captured differ across sources.

related.because: The failed invasion led to Operation Mongoose and pushed Cuba toward the Soviet Union, whose arms shipments culminated in the 1962 missile crisis (Office of the Historian).

reviewer_note: Pin is the bay, not a beach: the opened pages do not name Playa Girón or Playa Larga. Brigade size is 1,400 on the CIA page (other accounts say 1,400-1,500). Killed and captured totals are not on the Office of the Historian page; the CIA page gives more than 75 percent imprisoned and 1,113 held. Death count deliberately omitted. The 19 April end date is "within two days" and not a stated date.

beats.caption: Brigade 2506, a CIA-trained exile force launched from Guatemala, lands at the Bay of Pigs.
Without air support, the outnumbered brigade surrenders or withdraws into the water; more than three quarters end up in Cuban prisons.
Castro declares intent to adopt socialism, and Kennedy approves Operation Mongoose, a covert program aimed at removing him.
